# Project Goals: Website Redesign

As part of the initial phase of the **Website Redesign** project, below is a defined set of strategic goals, operational objectives, and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). These goals establish clear direction, align design and technical efforts, and provide measurable benchmarks for project success.

---

## Strategic Goals & Objectives

### 1. Enhance User Experience (UX) & Visual Design (UI)
* **Objective:** Modernize the website’s visual aesthetics to align with contemporary design standards and brand identity.
* **Key Focus Areas:**
  * Implement an intuitive, friction-free navigation structure.
  * Establish a cohesive design system (color palette, typography, UI components).
  * Ensure full responsiveness and seamless experience across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.

### 2. Improve Conversions & User Engagement
* **Objective:** Optimize user journeys to encourage visitors to take desired actions (e.g., contact forms, newsletter sign-ups, purchases, demo requests).
* **Key Focus Areas:**
  * Design strategic, clear, and compelling Call-to-Action (CTA) elements.
  * Reduce form fields and friction in lead generation/checkout paths.
  * Create tailored landing pages for high-value user personas.

### 3. Enhance Technical Performance & Accessibility
* **Objective:** Build a fast, secure, and globally accessible web experience.
* **Key Focus Areas:**
  * Optimize core Web Vitals (improving page load time to under 2.5 seconds).
  * Achieve compliance with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1 Level AA).
  * Enforce robust security practices (SSL certification, data encryption, secure headers).

### 4. Strengthen SEO & Search Engine Visibility
* **Objective:** Maximize organic search traffic and preserve/improve search engine rankings during and after the redesign.
* **Key Focus Areas:**
  * Execute a comprehensive 301 redirect map to preserve existing URL authority.
  * Implement clean site architecture, XML sitemaps, and structured schema markup.
  * Optimize on-page metadata, image alt tags, and mobile-first indexing compliance.

### 5. Streamline Content Management & Maintainability
* **Objective:** Empower internal teams to easily update, manage, and publish content without relying heavily on technical support.
* **Key Focus Areas:**
  * Implement a user-friendly Content Management System (CMS) or modular page-building architecture.
  * Create reusable content blocks and templates.
  * Establish clear content workflows and editorial permissions.

---

## Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for Success

To measure the success of the website redesign post-launch, progress will be tracked against the following targets:

| Metric Category | Target KPI Benchmark |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Site Speed / Performance** | Page load time < 2.5s; Google PageSpeed score > 85/100 (Mobile & Desktop) |
| **User Engagement** | 15% reduction in Bounce Rate; 20% increase in Average Session Duration |
| **Conversion Rate** | 20–30% increase in overall conversion rate across key user funnels |
| **SEO / Organic Traffic** | Maintain zero organic ranking loss post-launch; 15% growth in organic impressions within 90 days |
| **Accessibility** | 100% pass rate on WCAG 2.1 AA automated audit tools |

---

## Next Steps
1. Review and validate these project goals with key stakeholders.
2. Translate these goals into initial technical requirements and wireframe design briefs.
3. Begin defining user personas and content architecture based on these goals.

# Project Requirements Research & Analysis Specification

**Project Name:** Test Project  
**Task:** Research Requirements  
**Prepared By:** Assistly AI  

---

## 1. Executive Summary
This document presents the detailed requirements research and analysis for **Test Project**, directly building upon the foundational goals and SMART objectives established in the *Project Goals & Objectives Specification*. 

The objective of this research is to define, categorize, and specify functional, non-functional, technical, and operational requirements needed to achieve 100% scope readiness, ensure zero critical defects, and facilitate seamless project execution.

---

## 2. Methodology & Information Gathering
The research and synthesis of requirements were conducted through a structured analysis framework focused on standard project execution baselines, operational standards, and stakeholder deliverable needs.

```
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
       |             Requirements Research Framework           |
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
                                   |
        +--------------------------+--------------------------+
        |                                                     |
        v                                                     v
+-------------------------------+             +-------------------------------+
|    Functional Requirements    |             |  Non-Functional Requirements  |
|  - Workflow & Task Execution  |             |  - Performance & Pacing       |
|  - Progress & Status Tracking |             |  - Quality & Error Limits     |
|  - Documentation & Reporting  |             |  - Security & Governance      |
+-------------------------------+             +-------------------------------+
```

---

## 3. Categorized Project Requirements

### 3.1 Functional Requirements (FR)
Functional requirements define the specific behaviors, capabilities, and outputs required from the system/project deliverables.

| Req ID | Requirement Name | Description | Priority | Target Milestone |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **FR-01** | Task Management Baseline | The project framework must support explicit definition, assignment, and status tracking for all project tasks. | High | Phase 1 |
| **FR-02** | Output Verification | Every completed task deliverable must undergo a formal quality verification check prior to final sign-off. | High | Continuous |
| **FR-03** | Artifact Repository | A centralized documentation repository must store all project specs, deliverables, and operational logs. | Medium | Phase 1 |
| **FR-04** | Progress Reporting | Systematic tracking must generate accurate completion metrics and KPI reports (e.g., on-time completion rate). | Medium | Continuous |
| **FR-05** | Traceability Engine | Requirements must be mapped directly to project goals and verification checks through a Traceability Matrix. | High | Phase 2 |

---

### 3.2 Non-Functional Requirements (NFR)
Non-functional requirements specify performance, quality criteria, and operational constraints aligned with established KPIs.

#### A. Quality & Accuracy
* **NFR-QA-01 (Defect Tolerance):** Zero critical defects or standard non-compliances allowed on core task outputs.
* **NFR-QA-02 (First-Time Pass Rate):** Deliverables must achieve a $\ge 90\%$ initial pass rate during quality reviews.

#### B. Execution & Schedule Efficiency
* **NFR-SE-01 (Schedule Adherence):** Milestone tasks must maintain an on-time completion rate of $\ge 95\%$.
* **NFR-SE-02 (Turnaround Time):** Deliverable reviews and feedback loops must be resolved within standard project review cycles.

#### C. Documentation & Usability
* **NFR-DU-01 (Standardization):** All generated documentation must adhere to standardized markdown structure, professional formatting, and objective-aligned sectioning.
* **NFR-DU-02 (Completeness):** 100% of defined task outputs must be fully documented with clear operational instructions and outcomes.

---

### 3.3 Technical & Operational Requirements
* **TR-01 (Platform Standards):** Deliverables must be formatted for compatibility with standard document markdown standard specifications.
* **OR-01 (Process Governance):** Task execution must strictly align with the established 4-point SMART Objectives (Operational Readiness, Quality Standards, Schedule Efficiency, Stakeholder Alignment).

---

## 4. Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM)

This matrix maps researched requirements directly back to the SMART Project Goals defined in Task 1.

| Goal / SMART Objective | Requirement ID | Requirement Description | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Objective 1: Operational Readiness** | FR-01, FR-03, OR-01 | Task baseline, centralized repository, and standard workflows. | Scope readiness review & audit |
| **Objective 2: Quality Assurance** | FR-02, NFR-QA-01, NFR-QA-02 | Quality verification checks, zero critical errors, 90%+ pass rate. | First-submission quality review |
| **Objective 3: Schedule & Efficiency** | FR-04, NFR-SE-01, NFR-SE-02 | On-time tracking, $\ge 95\%$ adherence rate. | Task status & schedule log |
| **Objective 4: Stakeholder Alignment** | FR-05, NFR-DU-01, NFR-DU-02 | Requirements traceability, complete standardized artifacts. | Artifact audit & sign-off log |

---

## 5. Constraints, Assumptions, and Risk Factors

### Assumptions
1. Project execution will proceed sequentially based on established task dependencies.
2. Requirements are stable; minor modifications will be governed by standard review processes.

### Constraints
1. Work outputs must rely entirely on verified context, previous deliverables, and defined operational goals.
2. Deliverable timelines must strict adherence to the project pacing target ($\ge 95\%$).

### Risk Mitigation Plan
* **Risk:** Quality defects causing review delays.  
  * **Mitigation:** Implement strict pre-submission checklists mapped to NFR-QA-01.
* **Risk:** Unmapped requirements leading to scope creep.  
  * **Mitigation:** Maintain the Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) across all future project tasks.

---

## 6. Next Steps
1. Transition to detailed task execution and implementation based on verified functional requirements.
2. Utilize the Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) during deliverable verification checks.
3. Monitor ongoing task outputs against the NFR standards established in this specification.

## 1. Executive Summary & Project Objective
The objective of this task is to establish a comprehensive Business Requirements Framework for the **E-Commerce Website** project. This document defines key operational and functional specifications across target audience demographics, product catalog organization, payment processing options, and fulfillment/shipping mechanics. 

---

## 2. Target Audience & Customer Profiles

### 2.1 Primary Demographics & Segmentation
* **Target Segments:** Retail Consumers (B2C) with optional foundation for Wholesale/Business Accounts (B2B).

---

## 3. Product Catalog Structure & Taxonomy

### 3.1 Catalog Architecture
* **Hierarchy Depth:** 3-Tier Category Structure (`Root Category` > `Subcategory` > `Child/L3 Category`).
* **Product Types Supported:**
  1. **Simple Products:** Standalone physical items with fixed SKU and price.
  2. **Configurable / Variant Products:** Products with attributes (e.g., Size, Color, Material, Style) maintaining distinct inventory SKUs per variant combination.
  3. **Bundled / Kit Products:** Grouped items sold together at a combined rate.
  4. **Digital / Downloadable Products (Optional):** Non-physical items requiring instant delivery.

### 3.2 Product Attribute Matrix
| Attribute Group | Standard Attributes |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Core Identifiers** | SKU, Universal Product Code (UPC/EAN), Product Name, Short Description, Full Description. |

| **Media** | Primary Thumbnail, High-Res Gallery Images, Video Embeds, 360 Degree Views. |

---

## 4. Payment Gateway & Financial Specifications

### 4.1 Payment Gateway Requirements
* **Primary Processor Support:** Stripe / PayPal Complete Payments / Adyen / Authorize.net integration.
* **Supported Payment Methods:**
  * **Credit/Debit Cards:** Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover.
  * **Digital Wallets:** Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal Express Checkout.
  * **Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL):** Klarna / Affirm / Afterpay integration.
* **Security & Compliance:**
  * Full PCI-DSS Compliance (Tokenization via hosted fields/iFrames; no raw card data stored on local servers).
  * 3D Secure 2.0 (3DS2) authentication for fraud protection.
  * Automated TLS/SSL encryption for end-to-end data transfer.

### 4.2 Multi-Currency & Tax Engine Integration
* **Tax Calculation:** Automated real-time sales tax calculation via Avalara / TaxJar integration based on customer shipping address (destination-based taxation).
* **Currency Handling:** Base store currency with optional automated display conversion for targeted international regions.

---

## 5. Shipping & Order Fulfillment Specifications

### 5.1 Shipping Calculation Rules
* **Flat Rate Shipping:** Fixed rate applied per order, item, or weight class.
* **Tiered / Threshold Shipping:** Free shipping unlocked when cart total reaches a predefined amount (e.g., *Free Shipping on orders over $75*).
* **Real-Time Carrier Rates:** Live API rates calculated via USPS, FedEx, UPS, or DHL based on total weight, package dimensions, and origin-destination ZIP codes.
* **Geographic Zones:** Defined shipping zones (Local/Domestic, Regional, Rest of Country, International).

### 5.2 Order Fulfillment & Processing Logic
1. **Order Capture:** Order status set to `Pending Payment` -> `Processing` upon successful gateway authorization.
2. **Inventory Allocation:** Immediate stock deduction upon order placement; automated stock restoration upon cancellation.
3. **Fulfillment Integration:** Sync with Warehouse Management System (WMS) or 3PL system via API.
4. **Dispatch & Tracking:** Automated transactional email sent to customer with tracking number and carrier link upon generating shipping label (`Status: Shipped`).

To tailor the specific technical setup for implementation, please confirm or select preferred defaults for the following parameters:

1. **Product Catalog Size:** What is the estimated initial catalog size (e.g., <500 SKUs, 500–5,000 SKUs, >10,000 SKUs)?

4. **Tax Strategy:** Will tax calculation be handled via simple built-in state tax tables or an external service (e.g., TaxJar/Avalara)?

## 3. Inventory & Product Database Schema Design

The following PostgreSQL database schema is engineered using **Prisma ORM notation** (translatable to raw DDL SQL). It supports multi-tier categories, dynamic product attributes, variant-level SKUs, multiple warehouse/stock locations, and real-time inventory tracking logs.

```prisma
// datasource and generator configuration
datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

// ==========================================
// 1. PRODUCT CATALOG & TAXONOMY SCHEMA
// ==========================================

model Category {
  id             String     @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  parentId       String?    @map("parent_id") @db.Uuid
  name           String     @db.VarChar(255)
  slug           String     @unique @db.VarChar(255)
  description    String?    @db.Text
  isActive       Boolean    @default(true) @map("is_active")
  createdAt      DateTime   @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt      DateTime   @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  // Hierarchical Self-Relation
  parent         Category?  @relation("CategoryHierarchy", fields: [parentId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  children       Category[] @relation("CategoryHierarchy")
  
  products       ProductCategory[]

  @@index([parentId])
  @@index([slug])
  @@map("categories")
}

model Product {
  id             String            @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  sku            String            @unique @db.VarChar(100) // Base Product SKU
  name           String            @db.VarChar(255)
  slug           String            @unique @db.VarChar(255)
  description    String?           @db.Text
  basePrice      Decimal           @map("base_price") @db.Decimal(12, 2)
  costPrice      Decimal?          @map("cost_price") @db.Decimal(12, 2)
  status         ProductStatus     @default(DRAFT)
  taxClass       String            @default("STANDARD") @map("tax_class") @db.VarChar(50)
  createdAt      DateTime          @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt      DateTime          @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  categories     ProductCategory[]
  variants       ProductVariant[]
  images         ProductMedia[]

  @@index([slug])
  @@index([status])
  @@map("products")
}

enum ProductStatus {
  DRAFT
  ACTIVE
  ARCHIVED
}

model ProductCategory {
  productId  String   @map("product_id") @db.Uuid
  categoryId String   @map("category_id") @db.Uuid

  product    Product  @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  category   Category @relation(fields:categoryId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@id([productId, categoryId])
  @@map("product_categories")
}

model ProductMedia {
  id         String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  productId  String   @map("product_id") @db.Uuid
  url        String   @db.VarChar(500)
  altText    String?  @map("alt_text") @db.VarChar(255)
  sortOrder  Int      @default(0) @map("sort_order")
  isPrimary  Boolean  @default(false) @map("is_primary")

  product    Product  @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([productId])
  @@map("product_media")
}

// ==========================================
// 2. PRODUCT VARIANTS & ATTRIBUTES SCHEMA
// ==========================================

model Attribute {
  id         String            @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  name       String            @unique @db.VarChar(100) // e.g. Color, Size
  code       String            @unique @db.VarChar(100) // e.g. color, size
  
  options    AttributeOption[]

  @@map("attributes")
}

model AttributeOption {
  id          String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  attributeId String   @map("attribute_id") @db.Uuid
  value       String   @db.VarChar(100) // e.g. Red, XL
  code        String   @db.VarChar(100) // e.g. red, xl

  attribute   Attribute @relation(fields: [attributeId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  variants    VariantAttributeValue[]

  @@unique([attributeId, value])
  @@map("attribute_options")
}

model ProductVariant {
  id             String     @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  productId      String     @map("product_id") @db.Uuid
  sku            String     @unique @db.VarChar(100) // Distinct Variant SKU
  barcode        String?    @unique @db.VarChar(100) // UPC/EAN
  price          Decimal    @db.Decimal(12, 2)
  compareAtPrice Decimal?   @map("compare_at_price") @db.Decimal(12, 2)
  weight         Decimal?   @db.Decimal(8, 2) // In Kg or Lbs
  weightUnit     String     @default("LB") @map("weight_unit") @db.VarChar(10)
  isActive       Boolean    @default(true) @map("is_active")
  createdAt      DateTime   @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt      DateTime   @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  product        Product    @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  attributeValues VariantAttributeValue[]
  inventoryLevels InventoryLevel[]
  orderItems     OrderItem[]

  @@index([productId])
  @@index([sku])
  @@map("product_variants")
}

model VariantAttributeValue {
  variantId         String          @map("variant_id") @db.Uuid
  attributeOptionId String          @map("attribute_option_id") @db.Uuid

  variant           ProductVariant  @relation(fields: [variantId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  attributeOption   AttributeOption @relation(fields: [attributeOptionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@id([variantId, attributeOptionId])
  @@map("variant_attribute_values")
}

// ==========================================
// 3. INVENTORY MANAGEMENT & WAREHOUSING
// ==========================================

model Location {
  id          String           @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  name        String           @db.VarChar(255) // e.g. Warehouse East, Store #102
  code        String           @unique @db.VarChar(50)
  address     String           @db.VarChar(255)
  city        String           @db.VarChar(100)
  state       String           @db.VarChar(100)
  postalCode  String           @map("postal_code") @db.VarChar(20)
  country     String           @db.VarChar(2) // ISO Code
  isPrimary   Boolean          @default(false) @map("is_primary")

  inventory   InventoryLevel[]
  logs        InventoryLog[]

  @@map("locations")
}

model InventoryLevel {
  id             String         @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  variantId      String         @map("variant_id") @db.Uuid
  locationId     String         @map("location_id") @db.Uuid
  availableQty   Int            @default(0) @map("available_qty")
  reservedQty    Int            @default(0) @map("reserved_qty") // Reserved for pending orders
  reorderPoint   Int            @default(10) @map("reorder_point")

  variant        ProductVariant @relation(fields: [variantId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  location       Location       @relation(fields: [locationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([variantId, locationId])
  @@index([variantId])
  @@map("inventory_levels")
}

model InventoryLog {
  id            String            @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  variantId     String            @map("variant_id") @db.Uuid
  locationId    String            @map("location_id") @db.Uuid
  quantityDelta Int               @map("quantity_delta") // + / - change amount
  type          InventoryLogType
  referenceId   String?           @map("reference_id") @db.VarChar(255) // e.g. Order ID or Restock ID
  notes         String?           @db.Text
  createdAt     DateTime          @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  location      Location          @relation(fields: [locationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([variantId])
  @@index([locationId])
  @@map("inventory_logs")
}

enum InventoryLogType {
  PURCHASE_RESTOCK
  ORDER_RESERVATION
  ORDER_FULFILLMENT
  CANCELLATION_RESTOCK
  MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT
  DAMAGE_LOSS
}

// ==========================================
// 4. ORDER TRANSACTIONS (SCHEMA LINK)
// ==========================================

model OrderItem {
  id          String         @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  orderId     String         @map("order_id") @db.Uuid
  variantId   String         @map("variant_id") @db.Uuid
  unitPrice   Decimal        @map("unit_price") @db.Decimal(12, 2)
  quantity    Int

  variant     ProductVariant @relation(fields: [variantId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)

  @@index([orderId])
  @@map("order_items")
}
```

## 4. Key Architectural & Technical Highlights

1. **High-Performance Querying:**  
   - Indexed database fields on `slug`, `sku`, `status`, and foreign keys guarantee millisecond responses for product dynamic lookup and route rendering.
2. **ACID-Compliant Multi-Location Inventory Allocation:**  
   - Inventory separation between `availableQty` and `reservedQty` prevents overselling during checkout spikes.
   - Row-level transactions are logged in `InventoryLog` for real-time reporting and WMS sync.
3. **Decoupled Architecture Scalability:**  
   - Next.js static page generation combined with dynamic API endpoints on Redis/Node.js ensures sub-second paint times on mobile, reducing cart abandonment.
